extracted.intended_audience: CJR-X participants and collaborators (ACOs, PGPs, NPPGPs, TGPs), collaboration agents and downstream collaboration agents, SNFs, Medicare compliance officers, and program implementers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards for CJR‑X sharing, distribution, downstream distribution arrangements, beneficiary incentives, documentation, applicable safe harbors, and selected Medicare program waivers (telehealth, SNF 3‑day rule, post‑discharge home visits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written and signed distribution arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: All distribution arrangements must be in writing and signed by the parties, contain the effective date of the agreement, and be entered into before care is furnished to CJR‑X beneficiaries under the distribution arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(1). Requires contemporaneous, pre‑existing written agreements prior to furnishing care under the arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary participation in distribution arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in a distribution arrangement must be voluntary and without penalty for nonparticipation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(2). Programs must not coerce collaboration agents into accepting distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and regulatory compliance by collaboration agents
rubrics_metrics.description: The distribution arrangement must require the collaboration agent to comply with all applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(3). Includes fraud and abuse laws and other applicable statutory/regulatory duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: No conditioning on volume or value of referrals for distribution arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The opportunity to make or receive a distribution payment must not be conditioned directly or indirectly on the volume or value of past or anticipated referrals or business otherwise generated by, between or among the CJR‑X participant, any CJR‑X collaborator, any collaboration agent, any downstream collaboration agent, or any affiliated individual or entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(4). Prohibits any direct or indirect linkage between distributions and referral volume/value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution payment methodology based solely on quality and CJR‑X activities (ACOs/NPPGPs/TGPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of any distribution payments from an ACO, from an NPPGP to an NPPGP member, or from a TGP to a TGP member, must be determined in accordance with a methodology that is solely based on quality of care and the provision of CJR‑X activities and that may take into account the amount of such CJR‑X activities provided by a collaboration agent relative to other collaboration agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(5). Payment formulas must use quality and CJR‑X activity metrics only; relative contribution may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution payment methodology based solely on quality and CJR‑X activities (PGPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of any distribution payments from a PGP must be determined in accordance with a methodology that is solely based on quality of care and the provision of CJR‑X activities and that may take into account the amount of such CJR‑X activities provided by a collaboration agent relative to other collaboration agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(6). Same standard as for ACOs/NPPGPs/TGPs, stated separately for PGPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to receive distribution payment tied to furnishing/billing during attributed episode
rubrics_metrics.description: A collaboration agent is eligible to receive a distribution payment only if the collaboration agent furnished or billed for an item or service rendered to a CJR‑X beneficiary during an episode that was attributed to the same performance year for which the CJR‑X participant accrued the internal cost savings or earned the reconciliation payment amount that comprises the gainsharing payment being distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(7). Ensures payments go only to those who actually provided/billed services in the relevant attributed episodes and performance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap on total distribution payments (not to exceed gainsharing payment)
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to the distribution of any gainsharing payment received by an ACO, PGP, NPPGP, or TGP, the total amount of all distribution payments for a performance year must not exceed the amount of the gainsharing payment received by the CJR‑X collaborator from the CJR‑X participant for the same performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(8). Aggregate distributions cannot exceed the original gainsharing funds received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traceable form of distribution payments
rubrics_metrics.description: All distribution payments must be made by check, electronic funds transfer, or another traceable cash transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(9). Cash or non‑traceable transfers are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration agent clinical decision‑making independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The collaboration agent must retain the ability to make decisions in the best interests of the patient, including the selection of devices, supplies, and treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(10). Payment arrangements must not interfere with clinical autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution arrangements must not reduce medically necessary care or reward unnecessary care
rubrics_metrics.description: The distribution arrangement must not (i) induce the collaboration agent to reduce or limit medically necessary items and services to any Medicare beneficiary or (ii) reward the provision of items and services that are medically unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(11). Explicit anti‑inducement and anti‑overutilization prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for distribution arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJR‑X collaborator must maintain contemporaneous documentation regarding distribution arrangements in accordance with §512.135, including the relevant written agreements; the date and amount of any distribution payment(s); the identity of each collaboration agent that received a distribution payment; and a description of the methodology and accounting formula for determining the amount of any distribution payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(12). Requires specific items of contemporaneous documentation for audits and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on entering distribution arrangement with parties who have sharing arrangement with same participant
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJR‑X collaborator may not enter into a distribution arrangement with any individual or entity that has a sharing arrangement with the same CJR‑X participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(13). Prevents duplicative or conflicting sharing/distribution chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation access and retention for distribution arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJR‑X collaborator must retain and provide access to, and must require collaboration agents to retain and provide access to, the required documentation in accordance with §512.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.675(b)(14). Requires both retention and provision of access to documentation by collaborators and agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream distribution arrangements must be in writing and pre‑existing
rubrics_metrics.description: All downstream distribution arrangements must be in writing and signed by the parties, contain the effective date of the agreement, and be entered into before care is furnished to CJR‑X beneficiaries under the downstream distribution arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(1). Mirror of distribution arrangement timing/formation rules for downstream arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary participation in downstream distribution arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in a downstream distribution arrangement must be voluntary and without penalty for nonparticipation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(2). No coercion of downstream collaboration agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and regulatory compliance by downstream collaboration agents
rubrics_metrics.description: The downstream distribution arrangement must require the downstream collaboration agent to comply with all applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(3). Same compliance obligation applied to downstream agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: No conditioning on volume or value of referrals for downstream distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The opportunity to make or receive a downstream distribution payment must not be conditioned directly or indirectly on the volume or value of past or anticipated referrals or business otherwise generated among the relevant parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(4). Prohibits tying downstream payments to referrals/business volume/value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream distribution payment methodology based on quality and CJR‑X activities (NPPGP/TGP→members)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of any downstream distribution payments from an NPPGP to an NPPGP member or from a TGP to a TGP member must be determined in accordance with a methodology that is solely based on quality of care and the provision of CJR‑X activities and that may take into account the amount of such CJR‑X activities provided by a downstream collaboration agent relative to other downstream collaboration agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(5). Mirrors the quality‑based payment methodology requirement for downstream payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream distribution payment methodology based on quality and CJR‑X activities (PGP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of any downstream distribution payments from a PGP must be determined in accordance with a methodology that is solely based on quality of care and the provision of CJR‑X activities and that may take into account the amount of such CJR‑X activities provided by a downstream collaboration agent relative to other downstream collaboration agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(6). Stated separately for PGPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for downstream distribution payments tied to furnishing during attributed episode
rubrics_metrics.description: A downstream collaboration agent is eligible to receive a downstream distribution payment only if the downstream collaboration agent furnished an item or service to a CJR‑X beneficiary during an episode that is attributed to the same performance year for which the CJR‑X participant accrued the internal cost savings or earned the reconciliation payment amount that comprises the gainsharing payment from which the ACO made the distribution payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(7). Requires actual service provision within attributed episode/performance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap on total downstream distribution payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The total amount of all downstream distribution payments made to downstream collaboration agents must not exceed the amount of the distribution payment received by the PGP, NPPGP, or TGP from the ACO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(8). Ensures downstream payments are limited to funds received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traceable form of downstream distribution payments
rubrics_metrics.description: All downstream distribution payments must be made by check, electronic funds transfer, or another traceable cash transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(9). Same traceability requirement as for distribution payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream collaboration agent clinical decision‑making independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The downstream collaboration agent must retain his or her ability to make decisions in the best interests of the beneficiary, including the selection of devices, supplies, and treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(10). Protects clinical autonomy for downstream agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream arrangements must not reduce necessary care or reward unnecessary care
rubrics_metrics.description: The downstream distribution arrangement must not (i) induce the downstream collaboration agent to reduce or limit medically necessary services to any Medicare beneficiary or (ii) reward the provision of items and services that are medically unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(11). Anti‑inducement and anti‑overuse rule for downstream arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for downstream distribution arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PGP, NPPGP, or TGP must maintain contemporaneous documentation regarding downstream distribution arrangements in accordance with §512.135, including the relevant written agreements; the date and amount of any downstream distribution payment; the identity of each downstream collaboration agent that received a downstream distribution payment; and a description of the methodology and accounting formula for determining the amount of any downstream distribution payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(12). Specific documentation items required for downstream arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on downstream counterparties with existing sharing/distribution arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PGP, NPPGP, or TGP may not enter into a downstream distribution arrangement with any PGP member, NPPGP member, or TGP member who has (i) a sharing arrangement with a CJR‑X participant or (ii) a distribution arrangement with the ACO that the PGP, NPPGP, or TGP is a participant in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(13). Prevents conflicting or duplicative downstream chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation access and retention for downstream arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PGP, NPPGP, or TGP must retain and provide access to, and must require downstream collaboration agents to retain and provide access to, the required documentation in accordance with §512.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.680(b)(14). Mirrors documentation access/retention rule for downstream arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible in‑kind beneficiary engagement incentives (general conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants may choose to provide in‑kind patient engagement incentives including but not limited to items of technology to CJR‑X beneficiaries in an episode, subject to specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(a) preamble. Incentives are permitted only if all enumerated conditions are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct provision and control of beneficiary incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: The incentive must be provided directly by the CJR‑X participant or by an agent of the CJR‑X participant under the CJR‑X participant's direction and control to the CJR‑X beneficiary during an episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(a)(1). Third‑party uncontrolled giveaways are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical connection of incentive to care during episode
rubrics_metrics.description: The item or service provided must be reasonably connected to medical care provided to a CJR‑X beneficiary during an episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(a)(2). Incentives must have a reasonable clinical nexus to the episode's care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive must be preventive or advance clinical goal via engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The item or service must be a preventive care item or service or an item or service that advances a clinical goal for a CJR‑X beneficiary in an episode by engaging the CJR‑X beneficiary in better managing his or her own health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(a)(3). Incentives must either be preventive or support listed clinical goals by promoting beneficiary engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives cannot be tied to services outside the episode or to a particular provider
rubrics_metrics.description: The item or service must not be tied to the receipt of items or services outside the episode and must not be tied to the receipt of items or services from a particular provider or supplier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(a)(4)–(5). Prevents steering to outside services or specific providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: No advertising or promotion of incentive availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability of the items or services must not be advertised or promoted, except that a CJR‑X beneficiary may be made aware of the availability of the items or services at the time the CJR‑X beneficiary could reasonably benefit from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(a)(6). Limits outreach/marketing of incentives to non‑promotional notification when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of incentives must not be shifted to federal health care programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of the items and services must not be shifted to any federal health care program, as defined at section 1128B(f) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(a)(7). Prohibits billing federal programs for incentive costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology incentive retail value cap ($1,000 per episode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items or services involving technology provided to a CJR‑X beneficiary may not exceed $1,000 in retail value for any one CJR‑X beneficiary during any one episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(b)(1). Upper dollar limit for tech incentives per episode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology incentives must be minimum necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Items or services involving technology provided to a CJR‑X beneficiary must be the minimum necessary to advance a clinical goal for a beneficiary in an episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(b)(2). Technology must be narrowly tailored to clinical need/goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and retrieval requirement for higher‑value technology (> $75)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items of technology exceeding $75 in retail value must (i) remain the property of the CJR‑X participant; and (ii) be retrieved from the CJR‑X beneficiary at the end of the episode, with documentation of the ultimate date of retrieval. The CJR‑X participant must document all retrieval attempts and, if not retrievable, determine why and take steps to prevent future beneficiary incentives for that beneficiary if misappropriated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(b)(3). Documented, diligent, good faith retrieval attempts will be deemed to meet the retrieval requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical goals that incentives may advance
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X clinical goals that may be advanced through incentives: (1) beneficiary adherence to drug regimens; (2) beneficiary adherence to a care plan; (3) reduction of readmissions and complications following an episode; (4) management of chronic diseases and conditions that may be affected by the CJR‑X procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(c). Incentives should target these specified clinical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required for beneficiary incentives exceeding $25
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants must maintain documentation of items and services furnished as beneficiary incentives that exceed $25 in retail value, established contemporaneously and including at least the date the incentive is provided and the identity of the beneficiary to whom it was provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(d)(1)–(2). Contemporaneous recordkeeping required for monitoring and audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional documentation for technology over $75
rubrics_metrics.description: The documentation regarding items of technology exceeding $75 in retail value must also include contemporaneous documentation of any attempt to retrieve technology at the end of an episode, or why the items were not retrievable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(d)(3). Requires tracking retrieval attempts/reasons for non‑retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and access to incentive documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJR‑X participant must retain and provide access to the required documentation in accordance with §512.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.685(d)(4). Records must be available for inspection under §512.135 retention/access rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor availability if all requirements met
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS has determined that the Federal anti‑kickback statute safe harbor for CMS‑sponsored model arrangements (42 CFR 1001.952(ii)(1)) and the CMS‑sponsored model patient incentives safe harbor (42 CFR 1001.952(ii)(2)) is available to protect remuneration furnished in CJR‑X if the payments or incentives meet all safe harbor requirements set forth in 42 CFR 1001.952(ii) and the corresponding §§512.670, 512.675, 512.680, or 512.685.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.690. Protection from AKS prosecution depends on full compliance with both the safe harbor text and the corresponding CJR‑X provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of geographic site requirement for telehealth (limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives the geographic site requirements of section 1834(m)(4)(C)(i)(I) through (III) of the Act for episodes being tested in CJR‑X solely for services that may be furnished via telehealth under existing Medicare program requirements and are included in the episode in accordance with §512.625(e), except for geographic site requirements for a face‑to‑face encounter for home health certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(a)(1). Waiver applies only to telehealth‑eligible services included in the episode and excludes certain home health certification encounters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of originating site requirement for telehealth (home allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives the originating site requirements to permit a telehealth visit to originate in the beneficiary's home or place of residence solely for services that may be furnished via telehealth and are included in the episode per §512.625(e), except for originating site requirements for a face‑to‑face encounter for home health certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(a)(2). Authorizes home as originating site for covered telehealth services during CJR‑X episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selected telehealth payment provisions waived (facility fee/distant site payments)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives payment requirements so that the facility fee normally paid to an originating site is not paid if service originates in the beneficiary's home, and waives payment requirements to allow distant site payment for telehealth home visit HCPCS codes unique to CJR‑X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(a)(3). Payment exceptions limited to specified items; other telehealth payment rules continue to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: All other telehealth coverage/payment rules remain applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: All other requirements for Medicare coverage and payment of telehealth services continue to apply, including the list of specific services approved to be furnished by telehealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(a)(4). Only specified waivers are granted; standard telehealth rules and service lists still govern.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNF 3‑day rule waiver for qualified SNFs (anchor hospitalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives the SNF 3‑day rule for coverage of a SNF stay within 90 days of discharge from the anchor hospitalization for a beneficiary who is a CJR‑X beneficiary on the date of discharge if the SNF is identified on the applicable calendar quarter list of qualified SNFs at time of admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(b)(1). Waiver conditioned on SNF being on CMS's qualified list for the quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNF 3‑day rule waiver for anchor procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives the SNF 3‑day rule for coverage of a SNF stay within 90 days of the date of service of the anchor procedure for a CJR‑X beneficiary if the SNF is identified on the applicable calendar quarter list of qualified SNFs at time of admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(b)(2). Mirrors hospitalization waiver but keyed to anchor procedure dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for determination of qualified SNFs
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS determines the qualified SNFs for each calendar quarter based on a review of the most recent rolling 12 months of overall star ratings on the Five‑Star Quality Rating System for SNFs; qualified SNFs are rated an overall of 3 stars or better for at least 7 of the 12 months; providers furnishing SNF services under swing bed agreements are included and not subject to the star ratings requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(b)(3). Uses Nursing Home Compare star ratings and includes swing‑bed providers with special rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance posting of qualified SNFs list
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS posts to the CMS website the list of qualified SNFs in advance of the calendar quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(b)(4). Enables participants/beneficiaries to check SNF qualification status prior to admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial liability protections if SNF waiver requirements not met
rubrics_metrics.description: If CMS determines waiver requirements were not met: (i) CMS makes no payment to the SNF for SNF services if SNF admits a CJR‑X beneficiary without a qualifying anchor hospitalization or procedure; (ii) if CMS makes no payment, beneficiary protections apply unless the CJR‑X participant provided a discharge planning notice per §512.622(c): (A) the SNF must not charge beneficiary; (B) SNF must return monies collected for such services; (C) CJR‑X participant is financially liable for services; if the participant provided the required notice, normal SNF coverage requirements apply and the beneficiary may be financially liable for non‑covered SNF services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(b)(5)–(6). Establishes beneficiary protections and participant financial responsibility tied to issuance of required discharge planning notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of direct supervision requirement for certain post‑discharge home visits
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives the requirement that services furnished incident to a physician's service be furnished under direct supervision to permit certain home visits: applicable only when (i) the visit is during the episode to a CJR‑X beneficiary discharged from an anchor hospitalization or procedure; (ii) furnished at beneficiary's home; (iii) beneficiary does not qualify for home health services at the time; (iv) furnished by clinical staff under general supervision of a physician or non‑physician practitioner; and (v) no more than 9 visits furnished during the episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(c)(1)–(2). Defines the limited circumstances and supervision level (general rather than direct) allowed; services are not considered 'hospital services.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing/payment for permitted post‑discharge home visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 9 post‑discharge home visits per CJR‑X episode may be billed under Part B by the physician or nonphysician practitioner or by the CJR‑X participant to which the supervising physician has reassigned his or her billing rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(c)(3). Specifies who may bill for the permitted visits and the billing limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Medicare rules continue to apply to services incident to a physician's service
rubrics_metrics.description: All other Medicare rules for coverage and payment of services incident to a physician's service continue to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From §512.695(c)(4). Only the direct supervision requirement is waived in limited circumstances; other rules remain binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization basis for national standardized amount (IPPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The national standardized amount is based on per discharge averages of adjusted hospital costs from a base period, updated and otherwise adjusted in accordance with the provisions of section 1886(d) of the Act, with standardization to remove cost variations (case‑mix, area wages, COLA for AK/HI, IME, DSH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Addendum, 'Standardization of Base‑Year Costs or Target Amounts' discussion. Describes conceptual basis and statutory citations for standardization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equalization of standardized amounts for urban and other areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Equalization of the standardized amounts for urban and other areas at the level computed for large urban hospitals during FY 2004 and onward, as provided under section 1886(d)(3)(A)(iv)(II) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Addendum summary. National standardized amount computed at large urban level per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor‑related share application and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027, proposed labor‑related share of 66.0 percent for national standardized amounts for IPPS hospitals with wage index > 1.0000; apply wage index to a labor‑related share of 62 percent for hospitals with wage index ≤ 1.0000, consistent with section 1886(d)(3)(E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Addendum. Specifies different labor‑share treatment contingent on wage index thresholds and references statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating national standardized amount using market basket and productivity adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(b)(3)(B) specifies the applicable percentage increase used to update the standardized amount; for FY 2027 CMS proposes to use the 2023‑based IPPS operating and capital market baskets and to reduce the applicable percentage increase by the productivity adjustment (example forecast: 3.2% market basket, 0.8 percentage point productivity adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Addendum 'Updating the National Average Standardized Amount'. Reflects methodology and illustrative forecast numbers used in the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget‑neutrality adjustments to standardized amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments to the standardized amount will be made in a budget‑neutral manner to account for: DRG recalibration and reclassification; permanent 10‑percent cap on MS‑DRG relative weight reductions; wage index and labor‑related share changes; geographic reclassification; wage index cap policy; transition for discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy; removal/apply outlier offsets; rural floor budget neutrality adjustment; and treatment of the Stem Cell Acquisition Budget Neutrality Factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Addendum summary. Lists the specific budget neutrality adjustments CMS proposes or applies when computing national standardized amounts.
